earlier_scan.source_named: Only documentation per Glottolog is McCulloch 1859 wordlist; extinct, no phonological description exists

sources.citation: Huziwara, Keisuke. 2020. On the genetic position of Chakpa within Luish languages. Himalayan Linguistics 19(2): 44-57. doi:10.5070/H91150999.
sources.note: Nothing on Chairel prosody. Chairel data source is given as 'McCulloch (1859) modified by Huziwara'; fn. 8: Matisoff (2013:16) treats Chairel as Luish, Grierson (1927), Shafer (1970:390) and Huziwara (2014a) do not. Section 2.2.4 'Tones' treats Proto-Luish/Cak/Kadu/Ganan tones and says of the sister Manipur variety Chakpa that its tones 'are unknown as they are no longer spoken nor recorded' -- Chairel is not even included in the tone table.

sources.citation: 藤原敬介 [Huziwara, Keisuke]. 2016. 科学研究費助成事業 研究成果報告書 [KAKENHI final research report], 課題番号 25770154 (若手研究(B), 2013-2015: descriptive and historical study of the Luish languages). 4 pp.
sources.note: no phonology content; p. 3: '死語であるチャイレル語についても、のこされた語彙資料を精査し、チャクパ語との系統関係を考察する学会発表をおこない、チャクパ語とは同系統とはいえないと結論づけた' (for the dead Chairel language the surviving vocabulary material was examined, a conference paper on its relationship to Chakpa was given, concluding it cannot be called the same lineage as Chakpa). Pointer to work index 3 only.

sources.citation: 藤原敬介 [Huziwara, Keisuke]. 2014. ルイ祖語の再考 [Proto-Luish reconsidered]. 京都大学言語学研究 (Kyoto University Linguistic Research) 33: 1-32. hdl:2433/196280.
sources.note: fn. 1 (p. 1): Matisoff 2013 includes Chairel in Luish; earlier classifications rested on the ethnic label 'Lui', 'there is no linguistic evidence'; the author holds Chairel is certainly Sal but not demonstrably Luish, referring to 藤原 2014 (LSJ 148) and promising a separate paper. p. 2: Andro and Sengmai data are from McCulloch 1859, '声調は記録されていない' (tones not recorded); fn. 5: McCulloch's {u} vs {a} may encode a vowel-length difference but is not used consistently (藤原 2013b). Nothing on Chairel prosody.

sources.citation: Matisoff, James A. 2013. Re-examining the genetic position of Jingpho: putting flesh on the bones of the Jingpho/Luish relationship. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 36(2): 1-106.
sources.note: Discusses Chairel forms (p.16) within Jingpho-Luish; would confirm that nothing beyond McCulloch's list exists. No prosodic statement expected.

sources.citation: Matisoff, James A. 2012. Re-examining the genetic position of Jingpho: putting flesh on the bones of the Jingpho/Luish relationship. Paper for the conference 'Mainland Southeast Asian Languages: the State of the Art in 2012', Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology, Leipzig, 29 Nov-1 Dec 2012. 51 pp. (Glottolog reference 303599; conference version of Matisoff 2013, LTBA 36(2).)
sources.note: Nothing for Chairel (or Andro/Sengmai). The paper's tone material concerns Kadu (Sangdong 2012: four tones listed p. ~13), Sak/Cak, Lahu and Jingpho (appendix 'Tones' p. 48 is Jingpho's inventory); for a Jingpho dialect form it notes 'tones are unknown' (p. 38). a full-text search for stress/accent the extracted text for tone|tonal|stress|accent finds no line co-occurring with Chairel, Andro or Sengmai.

sources.citation: 藤原敬介 [Huziwara, Keisuke]. 2012. ルイ祖語の再構にむけて [Towards a reconstruction of Proto-Luish]. 京都大学言語学研究 (Kyoto University Linguistic Research) 31: 25-131. hdl:2433/182194.
sources.note: p. 26 fn. 2-3: 'さまざまな研究でアンドロ語、センマイ語、チャイレル語の資料としてしめされるものは、実質的にはすべてMcCulloch[1859]にしめされた資料からのまごびきである … チャイレル語の資料としてはMcCulloch[1859]しかなく、Benedict[1972:7]によるとすでに死語であるという' (everything cited anywhere as Andro/Sengmai/Chairel data is second-hand from McCulloch 1859; McCulloch 1859 is the only Chairel material; extinct per Benedict). pp. 30-31 (source list): Andro and Sengmai 'McCulloch[1859]による。声調は記録されていない' (tones were not recorded). Section 6 treats Proto-Luish tone from Cak/Kadu/Ganan only. Nothing on Chairel stress or tone -- and an explicit statement that no data beyond the 1859 wordlist exist.

sources.citation: Laishram Romen (Rohen) Khuman. 2001. চকপা চাইরেল খুন্থোকলোন [Chakpa Chairel Khunthoklon: an account of the settlement of the Chakpa of Chairel]. Chairel Khongnang Leikai, Manipur: the author. 101 pp. In Meitei (Bengali script). Digital Library of India item 2015.466617 (duplicate scan 2015.466286, 'Chakpa Chairen Khunthoklon'); source library Manipur University.
sources.note: no phonology content found: archive.org scanned (Bengali-script Meitei, legible) scanned for a language chapter or word list -- searches for লোন/লোল (language), চকপা লোন, ৱাহৈ (word), ভাষা, McCulloch, অন্দ্রো, সেকমাই give only the running head '-khunthoklon', the adverb লোন্না-লোন্না and single incidental mentions; narrative settlement history and legends. page scan not inspected one by one, so a short embedded word list cannot be fully excluded, but nothing prosodic is plausible.

sources.citation: Bradley, David. 1997. Tibeto-Burman languages and classification. In David Bradley (ed.), Papers in Southeast Asian Linguistics No. 14: Tibeto-Burman Languages of the Himalayas (Pacific Linguistics A-86), 1-72. Canberra: Australian National University. doi:10.15144/PL-A86.1.
sources.note: nothing for Chairel: 'None of these languages is well described' (p. 25); group-level typological line p. 24-25 ('All these languages are SOV, with substantial prefix and suffix morphology') has no prosody

sources.citation: Bernot, Lucien. 1967. Les Cak: contribution à l'étude ethnographique d'une population de langue loi. Paris: Éditions du Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique. 267 pp. (archive.org IA41549404_0005, collection 'theses-and-dissertations / leiden-university', unrestricted; PDF 15.9 MB with scanned text.)
sources.note: Nothing on Chairel. The six Chairel passages are: McCulloch's Loee 'parlent des langues différentes selon qu'il s'agit des Andro (écrit Undro), des Sengmai, Chairel et Meeyang'; Damant 1880 classing Andro, Sengmai and Chairel as Kuki-Chin, 'Quant aux Chairel, ils n'habitent que deux villages'; LSI 1928 grouping 'l'Andro, le Sengmai, le Chairel et le Kadu' as the Lui Group; Shafer's Luish section = Andro, Sengmai, Sak, Kadu, 'il fait du Chairel une section différente'; LSI 1904 'seules les langues Andro, Sengmai et Chairel étaient rassemblées dans un groupe Loi'. Not downloaded under the two-f…

sources.citation: Benedict, Paul K. 1940. Studies in Indo-Chinese phonology. Harvard Journal of Asiatic Studies 5(2): 101-127. (Read in the Digital Library of India scan of HJAS vol. 5, archive.org;ernet.dli.2015.142585, leaf 125; article identity inferred from volume, year and position -- the footnote style with numbered roots 'No. 19', 'No. 65 infra' matches this paper.)
sources.note: Nothing prosodic: a lexical-distribution footnote (roots for FIRE and SUN shared by Northern Naga, Bodo-Garo, Kachin and 'the so-called Luish group (vide G. A. Grierson, Kadu and its relatives, BSOS 2 (1921) 39-42)'), noting Andro/Sengmai final -l vs Kadu -n and classing Chairel t'ir 'iron' as a Kukish loan. scanned is rough ('stm' = sun, 't'tr' = t'ir).

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. 1921. Kadu and its relatives. Bulletin of the School of Oriental Studies, London Institution 2(1): 39-42. doi:10.1017/S0041977X00101818.
sources.note: Nothing about Chairel's sound system; Chairel is mentioned twice, both times to exclude it from the group under comparison. (The 1.8 MB / 30 MB PDF of the volume were not downloaded under the two-file budget; the two Chairel paragraphs were read in full online.)

sources.citation: Hodson, T. C. 1908. The Meitheis. London: David Nutt. (archive.org meitheis01hods)
sources.note: no language data; the one relevant sentence (p. ~10): 'While the advance of Meithei has obliterated the dialectical distinction of the Lois of Sengmai, Andro and Chairel, their religious customs have suffered less modification' -- i.e. the Chairel speech was already gone by 1908. Other Chairel mentions concern pottery and administration.

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. (ed.) 1904/1927. Linguistic Survey of India, vol. III pt. III (Kuki-Chin and Burma groups: 'Lui' section) and vol. I pt. I.
sources.note: Reprints/discusses McCulloch's Andro, Sengmai, Chairel material under 'Lui'; second-hand, but the only other early treatment; open on archive.org/dsal, not downloaded because it adds no independent Chairel data.

sources.citation: McCulloch, W. 1859. Account of the Valley of Munnipore and of the Hill Tribes; with a Comparative Vocabulary of the Munnipore and other Languages. Selections from the Records of the Government of India (Foreign Department) No. XXVII. Calcutta: Bengal Printing Company. (archive.org india.history.resource.92455)
sources.note: Nothing. The only primary record of Chairel: a Chairel column in the appendix 'Comparative Vocabulary' (printed pp. xvi ff., pp. ~100-124). The one-paragraph pronunciation key on the appendix's first page covers only vowel letters (a 'as in Italian', oo, u, o) and th/gh; words are in an English-based spelling with occasional macrons/breves/acute (e.g. 'Kunangé', 'Hē ga') but no systematic accent marking and no statement about accent or stress.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page chai1254 (Chairel) and English Wikipedia 'Chairel language'
sources.note: Nothing; both state the language is extinct and documented only by McCulloch's 1859 wordlist; Wikipedia lists Benedict 1972, Matisoff 2013, Huziwara 2014 (LSJ 148: 272-277), van Driem 2014 as classification literature only.

sources.citation: Huziwara, Keisuke. 2014. チャイレル語の系統再考 [On the genetic position of Chairel reconsidered]. 日本言語学会第148回大会予稿集: 272-277.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained

sources.note: The only paper devoted to Chairel; re-analyses McCulloch's 1859 transcriptions ('McCulloch (1859) modified by Huziwara'). It cannot contain a first-hand stress statement, but if anyone has commented on what McCulloch's sporadic diacritics might encode, it is here.
